_note: Past reports, scored against the actual print. expected = pre-report trade average; actual = USDA print. The build script grades every row with scripts/report_bands.py; there is no 'surprise' field to set by hand. Since 2026-10-10 the grade is the distance from the trade average: within 0.5% for a yield, 1% for production and 2% for stocks is in line; outside it, a supply figure above the average is bearish and below it bullish. The survey's low and high (from data/analyst-estimates.json) are printed beside the grade as context and do not change it. No trade estimate = not graded. gap_pct is computed by the build script, never typed here. Add a new block after each release.

history.reaction: Corn stocks printed 2.095 billion bushels, above the entire pre-report trade range (1.843–2.005B), not just the 1.918B average. A real miss: more old-crop corn was sitting in bins and elevators on September 1 than any surveyed analyst had guessed.
Soybean stocks printed 0.315 billion bushels, 2.8% under the 0.324B trade average, outside the 2% band, so graded bullish. It was still inside the survey's 0.304 to 0.349B range, near the bottom.

Wheat stocks printed 1.846 billion bushels. No trade estimate was on file to grade this against, the only survey found had a wheat figure that didn't reconcile against a cited WASDE number, so it was withheld rather than published. The print stands on the record; it just isn't scored.

USDA's first survey-based corn yield came in at 180.7, 2.3 under July and 1.3 under the trade's 182.0. More acres (planted up 1.4M to 96.7M) kept production near-record at 16.013B bu, but the market traded the yield cut and the 1.653B carryout (down from 1.79B): December corn settled up 15 cents at $4.78.

Soybean yield printed 52.7, a couple tenths under both July and the trade, effectively in line. The acreage add (planted up 1.4M to 86.8M) still makes 4.519B bu the largest soybean crop on record, and carryout ticked up to 320M. November beans settled up 12 cents at $11.84, riding corn's coattails more than their own numbers.

New-crop wheat carryout came in at 744M, 21M (2.7%) under the 765M trade average and 18M under May, so graded bullish; it was still inside the survey's 740 to 804M range, near the bottom. The cut came from a smaller Hard Red Winter crop (all-wheat production trimmed to 1,543M, yield 47.0); the season-average farm price was cut $0.50 to $6.00.
Old-crop carryout landed right on the trade guess, a non-event for corn.
New-crop carryout nudged up fractionally on old-crop demand tweaks; essentially unchanged at $4.40.
Old-crop beans unchanged from May and on top of the trade, no reaction.
New-crop beans held at 310, a hair under the trade, quietly friendly but no fireworks.
Old-crop wheat held at 935, just under the trade guess.
Smallest winter wheat crop in six decades on Southern Plains drought - July KC wheat ran limit-up and futures hit 2-yr highs.
Trade looked for a higher carryout; the tighter print pushed Nov beans to a 2-yr high near $12.
New-crop carryout landed near the trade guess - ample supply into 2027 capped the upside.
Old-crop carryout close to the trade estimate - little reaction.
Old-crop carryout in line - the week's move came from the new-crop sheets.

USDA put 2026/27 corn carryout at 1.567 billion bushels, 34M above the 1.533B trade average (Dow Jones survey, via DTN). No survey low or high is on file for this figure, so it is graded on the 2% band.

USDA put 2026/27 soybean carryout at 310M, 20M above the 290M trade average (Dow Jones survey, via DTN). Reuters' survey averaged 298M; the print was above that too. No survey low or high is on file for this figure, so it is graded on the 2% band.
